voice.summary: Warm, confident, sensory. Unhurried sentences, specific dishes, gracious hospitality. Premium but never stiff: a jewel-toned dining room that still feels like the neighborhood.
do: Lead with the senses: char, steam, butter, tang, smoke.
Sound like a gracious host: ‘we’ and ‘you’, never ‘patrons’.
Let one word per headline carry the gold-foil treatment.
Stay approachable. This is Little Elm, not a black-tie room.
dont: Claim halal, vegan, gluten-free, ‘authentic’, awards or family recipes.
Mention prices, happy hour, buffets, specials or opening dates.
Reach for palace cliches: maharajas, elephants, ‘a feast fit for a king’.
Put Hindi in Royal headlines; keep Hindi to the Bazaar voice.

Slow-cooked curries, smoke-kissed kababs and biryani sealed with steam: a menu made for long tables and second helpings.

menu.headline: The menu, quarter by quarter
menu.body: Begin in Starters Square, linger in the Tandoor Quarter, take the slow road down Biryani Boulevard and end on Sweet Street. Every dish is made to share, and every spice level is cooked to your taste.

story.headline: A table that travels
story.body: Our kitchen moves from Andhra-style fire to the smoky glow of the tandoor, from slow-sealed dum biryani to glossy, wok-tossed Indo-Chinese. It is a generous Indian table with many accents, set for our neighbors in Little Elm.

catering.headline: Celebrations, beautifully fed
catering.body: From birthdays and baby showers to housewarmings and office gatherings, let our kitchen cater the feast while you enjoy your guests. We plan vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes, spice levels and timing with you, one conversation at a time.

visit.headline: Find your way to us
visit.body: You’ll find us at 11851 FM 423, Suite 200, in Little Elm, a short drive from Frisco. Parking is ample and the welcome is warm. Come for a long lunch, an easy dinner or a celebration table.

reviews.headline: What our guests return for
reviews.body: Rather than borrow a guest’s words, we’ll share the honest gist. Across Google, Yelp and the delivery apps, guests return for the biryani, the butter chicken, the garlic naan and a team that welcomes them warmly.

gallery.headline: A feast for the eyes, first
gallery.body: Steam caught in warm light. Naan torn at the table. The char on a tikka, the gloss on a curry, the moment a biryani is unsealed. Linger here a while, then come and taste it in person.

order.headline: Take the evening home
order.body: Order online for pickup directly from our kitchen, or choose delivery through Uber Eats, DoorDash or Grubhub. Select your dishes and your spice level, and we will prepare everything with the same care as in our dining room.

faq.headline: Before you visit
faq.body: Directions, hours, ordering and catering, answered simply. For the questions that deserve a personal reply, such as dietary questions or seating a large party, please call us. We are always glad to talk.

aboutStory.headline: A generous table in Little Elm
aboutStory.body: Curry District sets a generous Indian table on FM 423 in Little Elm, and our menu travels far to fill it. There is Andhra-style fire: Karampodi Chicken, deep with chili, and Gongura Mutton Pulav, bright with tangy gongura leaves. There are North Indian tandoor classics: Tandoori Chicken and Chicken Tikka Kabab with charred edges, and garlic naan torn warm at the table. Our dum biryani is layered, sealed and slow-steamed, so the lid lifts on a cloud of fragrance. And for a playful turn, Indo-Chinese street favorites such as Gobi Manchurian and Chilli Paneer arrive glossy from the wok. We cook for the neighborhood: weeknight dinners, birthday tables and the friends you have been meaning to see. Choose your spice level, gather your people and stay a while.

socialCaptions.caption: Lift the lid slowly. Layered, sealed and steamed, our dum biryani is worth the pause.
Butter Chicken, velvet-rich and unhurried. Add garlic naan and let the evening slow down.
From the tandoor: Chicken Tikka Kabab, edges kissed with char.
Gongura Mutton Pulav: tangy gongura leaves, tender mutton and a pulav with real character. Andhra-style and unforgettable.
Date night, Little Elm edition: two plates, one shared garlic naan and nowhere else to be.
The table keeps growing: biryani in the middle, naan going around, everyone reaching at once.
Hosting this season? Let our kitchen cater the celebration while you enjoy your guests. Call us to plan.
Lamps lit, plates full, everyone home. Planning a Diwali gathering? Call us to plan your catering. 🪔
socialCaptions.factCheck: Schedule 2–3 weeks before Diwali (about 8 Nov 2026; verify the date). No offer or price implied.

socialCaptions.caption: Paneer Tikka Masala, Palak Paneer, Dal Makhani: the vegetarian side of our menu deserves its own spotlight.
Chilli Paneer, wok-tossed and glossy. The Indo-Chinese corner of our menu, served with confidence.
End on something sweet. Gulab Jamun, soft and syrup-soaked, is the quiet finale after all that fire.
